relationships.description: The channel or point of access reads, captures or updates the business information, as when a customer portal displays an Order or a mailroom registers an incoming Claim.
relationships.evidence: Channel documentation, screen inventories or intake procedures for the interface list the business object as information captured, displayed or updated at that touchpoint.

relationships.description: Information gathered at the channel is passed on into the business object, as when details submitted at a branch counter or portal populate a new Claim or Order record.
relationships.evidence: A value-stream or information-flow diagram, or the channel's intake procedure, shows data entered at the interface being handed off to create or populate the business object.

relationships.description: The channel is a point through which the business service is offered and reached, as when a call centre makes Claims Handling available to policyholders.
relationships.evidence: The service catalogue or service description lists the interface among the channels or contact points through which that business service can be requested.

relationships.description: The specific person, team or external organization uses the channel to reach the organization's services, as when a named corporate customer submits orders through a dedicated portal.
relationships.evidence: Channel usage agreements, customer onboarding records or access lists identify the named actor as a user of that interface.

relationships.description: Whoever occupies the responsibility position uses the channel to obtain services, as when anyone acting as Customer or Broker contacts the claims hotline.
relationships.evidence: Channel strategy documents or customer journey maps name the role as the intended audience or user segment of the interface.

relationships.description: Contact received through the channel sets the ongoing competency area to work, as when inquiries arriving at the customer portal are routed to the Customer Support function.
relationships.evidence: Routing rules or operating procedures for the interface state that requests arriving there are dispatched to the business function for handling.

relationships.description: A request arriving through the channel initiates an instance of the business process, as when a claim submitted at the branch counter starts the claims-intake process.
relationships.evidence: The process model shows a start event or initiating step tied to receipt of a request via the interface, or the channel's procedures say each submission opens a process case.

notes: flows-to toward a passive BusinessObject is non-standard ArchiMate (flow links behavior/active elements) and largely duplicates accesses. Triggers from an interface is not valid ArchiMate (triggering is between behaviors/events); triggering a BusinessFunction, which has no defined start, is especially doubtful—consider serves or assigned-to via the service instead.
